name: crea_settings
description: The model and effort level an admin picks for the AI moderation assistant, applied to every moderator. A single-row singleton with id = 1.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Always 1. Not generated — the row is created by the migration, and there is never a second one.

columns.name: model
columns.description: NULL means fall back to the model the environment names.

columns.name: effort
columns.description: NULL means disabled — no adaptive thinking. That is a value, not a missing setting.

columns.name: fast_mode
columns.description: The same model with faster output at premium pricing. Not every model supports it, so a rejected request is retried without it rather than failing.

notes: A singleton table. Both implementations must read id = 1 and write id = 1; an INSERT that lets the database choose an id creates a second settings row that nothing will ever read.
Two nullable columns whose NULL means something specific — 'use the environment default' and 'disabled'. Neither is 'unset', so an implementation must not substitute a default of its own on read.

Architecture.md puts dynamic settings in a settings table editable from the admin frontend. This is that table for one domain; whether gradido2 keeps a per-domain table or folds it into a general one is a design decision, not a data one.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json.
